en: The Apadāna of the Elder Pulinacaṅkamīya Naḷamāli Chapter 10 I was a young man named Nāga, a master of the Vedas and their branches. At that time, the Blessed One, the Teacher of the World, was dwelling in the city of Rājagaha. Having heard that the Buddha had arrived, I went to see him with great joy. I approached the Teacher, the one who brings happiness to the world, and paid homage at his feet. Then, having circumambulated him three times, I sat down to one side. Seated there, I spoke these words to the Blessed One: "O Great Sage, you are the best of those who know the Dhamma; you are the supreme physician for those afflicted by the disease of suffering. Then the Teacher, the Knower of the World, knowing my intention, preached the Dhamma to me, beginning with the topic of generosity. Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I developed a mind of faith and offered a handful of sand to the Blessed One. Having made this offering, I took refuge in the Three Jewels. Then, having performed this deed, I passed away and was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-three gods. There, for eighty-four thousand aeons, I enjoyed celestial pleasures. When that aeon ended, I passed away from there and was reborn in the human world. There, for twenty thousand aeons, I lived as a king, a lord of the earth. Having enjoyed the fruit of that deed, I attained the state of a stream-enterer. I have now reached the end of suffering; I am a sage who has transcended birth. This is the unsurpassed fruit of the gift of sand. Thus did the Elder Pulinacaṅkamīya speak of his own past deeds.
“In the past, I was a deer-hunter in the forest wilderness,
searching for the wind-deer.”
I saw a walking path.
Taking sand from the hollow of my hand,
I scattered it upon the walking path.
With a serene mind and joyful heart,
[I offered] to the glorious Sugata.
Thirty-one eons ago from now,
I scattered sand;
I do not know a state of woe—
this is the fruit of that sand.
The defilements have been burnt away by me; ... [as before] ...
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges...
[as above] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Pulīnacankamiya spoke these verses.
This is the tenth legend of the elder Pulīnacankamiya.
The forty-eighth chapter, the Naḷamāli-vagga, is concluded.
Its summary verse:
Naḷamālī, Maṇidada,
Ukkā, Sati, Kabījanī;
Kummāsa and kusaṭṭha,
and also giripunnāgiya;
vallikāra and pānadhita.
And then the Pulinacaṅkama;
ninety-five verses have been counted by those who possess clear insight.
